Section 256.11, subsection 19, Code 2026, is amended 2 by adding the following new paragraph: 3 NEW PARAGRAPH . c. “Success-sequence education” means 4 instruction that addresses all of the following: 5 (1) The series of evidence-based, sequential milestones to 6 be accomplished prior to having children that has been shown to 7 help young adults achieve financial prosperity, physical and 8 mental health, and emotional well-being, including all of the 9 following: 10 (a) Obtaining at least a high school diploma. 11 (b) Securing full-time employment. 12 (c) Getting married. 13 (2) The evidence-based research indicating that marriage 14 generally provides financial, emotional, and health benefits to 15 the married individual and the married individual’s children. 16 (3) The evidence-based research indicating that children 17 with divorced parents generally have an increased likelihood 18 of poverty and incarceration and an increased risk of negative 19 physical and mental health outcomes. 20 Sec. 7. STATE MANDATE FUNDING SPECIFIED. In accordance 21 with section 25B.2, subsection 3, the state cost of requiring 22 compliance with any state mandate included in this Act shall 23 be paid by a school district from state school foundation aid 24 received by the school district under section 257.16. This 25 specification of the payment of the state cost shall be deemed 26 to meet all of the state funding-related requirements of 27 section 25B.2, subsection 3, and no additional state funding 28 shall be necessary for the full implementation of this Act 29 by and enforcement of this Act against all affected school 30 districts. 31 EXPLANATION 32 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 33 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 34 This bill requires school districts, accredited nonpublic 35 -2- LSB 6759XC (3) 91 jda/jh 2/ 4 S.F. _____ schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools to 1 provide success-sequence education in grades 7 through 12. 2 The bill defines “success-sequence education” as instruction 3 that addresses the series of evidence-based, sequential 4 milestones to be accomplished prior to having children that has 5 been shown to help young adults achieve financial prosperity, 6 physical and mental health, and emotional well-being; the 7 evidence-based research indicating that marriage generally 8 provides financial, emotional, and health benefits to the 9 married individual and the married individual’s children; and 10 the evidence-based research indicating that children with 11 divorced parents generally have an increased likelihood of 12 poverty and incarceration and an increased risk of negative 13 physical and mental health outcomes. 14 The bill incorporates success-sequence education into 15 the social studies curriculum in grades seven and eight for 16 students enrolled in school districts and accredited nonpublic 17 schools. Additionally, the bill incorporates success-sequence 18 education into the health education curriculum and the 19 personal finance literacy curriculum in grades 9 through 12 for 20 students enrolled in school districts and accredited nonpublic 21 schools. The bill requires charter schools and innovation zone 22 schools to provide such social studies curriculum and personal 23 finance literacy curriculum. Current law requires charter 24 zone schools and innovation zone schools to provide the same 25 health curriculum as school districts and accredited nonpublic 26 schools. 27 The bill may include a state mandate as defined in Code 28 section 25B.3. The bill requires that the state cost of 29 any state mandate included in the bill be paid by a school 30 district from state school foundation aid received by the 31 school district under Code section 257.16. The specification 32 is deemed to constitute state compliance with any state mandate 33 funding-related requirements of Code section 25B.2.
